themes.title: Through Acts
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. The story of the early church — the Spirit's movement from Jerusalem to Rome.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with the disciples staring at the sky. What are you waiting on?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the angel ask 'why do you stand gazing?'

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for the Spirit today. Use Peter's vocabulary: dreams, visions, prophecy.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Peter cite Joel rather than explain the wind and fire?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read about teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, prayer. Which is dimmest in your life right now?
core_arc.ask_seed: How do different traditions read the early church's common life?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for someone you have written off.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Saul's blindness lead to insight?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about a category of people you've kept at arm's length.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Peter need a vision before going to a Gentile's house?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with the closed doors before the open one.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the Spirit forbid Paul before sending him?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for a person of a different worldview, with respect.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Paul use Athenian poetry to preach Christ?

themes.title: Advent
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. The four weeks of waiting. Hope, peace, joy, love. Pinned in season.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Light a candle. Pray about a darkness you wait in.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is light the central image of Advent?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray Isaiah's vision over a place of conflict.
core_arc.ask_seed: What kind of king is the Branch of Jesse?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with Mary's 'be it unto me.'
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is the messianic story announced first to Mary?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the Magnificat aloud. Whose lowly state needs lifting today?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is Mary's hymn one of reversal?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the nativity slowly. Notice it is full of named ordinary people.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why are shepherds the first to hear?

themes.title: Anxiety in Christ
themes.description: Two weeks in scripture's voice on fear, presence, and trust. Mirrors the Anxious Guided Path, slowed down across days.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Name one specific anxiety. Hand it to God in a sentence.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Paul mean by 'the peace of God'? How is it different from calm?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Step outside, or to a window. Notice one created thing without trying to feel anything about it.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus point to birds and lilies instead of arguing against worry?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray verse 4 slowly. Where in your week is the valley?
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean that the shepherd is with the sheep in the valley, not above it?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read 'fear not, for I am with thee' aloud. Substitute 'I' with your own name in the next line.
core_arc.ask_seed: How is 'I am with you' different from 'everything will be okay'?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Cast one care today. Hold no expectation about what happens next.
core_arc.ask_seed: Peter pairs casting cares with resisting the devil. Why those two together?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Tell God one true thing about your fear today, before you tell him anything else.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why do the psalms let the singer be afraid AND trust at the same time?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: No assignment. Sit with 'his compassions fail not. They are new every morning.'
core_arc.ask_seed: What does 'mercies new every morning' do to a tired person?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: What storm are you in? What would 'peace, be still' sound like inside it?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why do the disciples ask 'do you not care?' Is that question wrong?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the list of things that cannot separate you from God's love. Add one of your own at the end.
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul lists tribulation, distress, persecution, famine. Why include such concrete things?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Set a timer for two minutes. 'Be still, and know that I am God.' Just that.
core_arc.ask_seed: The psalm describes mountains shaking. Why does 'be still' belong in a psalm about chaos?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Receive a gift you didn't earn. Sit a moment with that idea before praying.
core_arc.ask_seed: Jesus' peace is 'not as the world gives.' What does the world's version of peace look like by contrast?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Come to God today as someone who is understood, not someone who has to explain.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Hebrews emphasize that the high priest 'sympathizes with our weakness'?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Name a weakness you wish was gone. Ask, instead, for sufficient grace within it.
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul says he 'gladly' boasts in weakness. Is that performance, or is something else happening?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: 'My soul is even as a weaned child.' Pray it as a place to land, not a thing to achieve.
core_arc.ask_seed: This psalm is only three verses. Why might brevity be part of its point?

themes.title: Reasons for Faith
themes.description: Two weeks in the passages Christians have turned to when asked why they believe: creation, fulfilled prophecy, the eyewitnesses, and the resurrection.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for gentleness and respect whenever you speak about your hope.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Peter say about how to give a reason for your hope?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Go outside or look out a window, and praise the maker.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Psalm 19 say creation tells us about God?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for making himself known.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Paul say can be known about God from creation?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for someone you know who is searching.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Paul make his case to the philosophers in Athens?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bring your honest questions, as Thomas brought his.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why did Luke and John say they wrote their Gospels?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read it slowly, and thank him for bearing our griefs.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does the New Testament read Isaiah 53?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Let the turn from anguish to praise in this psalm shape your prayer.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Psalm 22 connect to the crucifixion of Jesus?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for those who handed the gospel on to you.
core_arc.ask_seed: What witnesses to the resurrection does Paul list?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Praise the God who raised Jesus up.
core_arc.ask_seed: What evidence does Peter give that Jesus is Lord and Christ?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for boldness, and for those who are almost persuaded.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Paul defend his faith before King Agrippa?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to hear the scriptures point to him.
core_arc.ask_seed: What witnesses does Jesus name to support his claims?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for a word made more sure.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Peter stress that the apostles were eyewitnesses?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bring the hardest question you carry about suffering.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does God answer Job's questions about suffering?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for faith that rests on what God has said.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does scripture say about itself in 2 Timothy 3?

themes.title: When Hope Feels Far
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Scripture meets discouragement before it argues with it.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Notice that Elijah is fed and rested before God speaks. What do you need first today?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does God let Elijah sleep before correcting his theology?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Speak to your own soul today, not just to God.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean to question your own discouragement without dismissing it?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read it slowly. Notice the turn at verse 17.
core_arc.ask_seed: Asaph almost loses his footing. What turns it?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about an inner cracking — not to fix it, but to receive treasure inside it.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Paul list pressure, perplexity, persecution as ordinary?

themes.title: Honest Doubt
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Scripture welcomes questions; this challenge sits with the people in scripture who asked them.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray your honest 'I will not believe unless...' — and let it stand.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus meet Thomas's demand on its own terms?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray 'I believe; help my unbelief' as one prayer, not two.
core_arc.ask_seed: How can someone hold belief and unbelief at the same time?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read several chapters at once. Don't try to extract a lesson.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does God answer Job with questions instead of explanations?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Tell God what does not make sense to you about the world this week.
core_arc.ask_seed: Habakkuk's complaint becomes a hymn. What changed — the situation, or him?

themes.title: Easter Octave
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. The eight days from Easter Sunday through the following Sunday. Resurrection appearances.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hear your name spoken by the risen Christ.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is the first witness a woman, weeping?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Walk a road today (literal or otherwise) listening for him.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is recognition tied to the breaking of bread?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about a fear that has you behind a locked door.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the risen Christ keep his wounds?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Receive a restoration.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus mirror Peter's three denials with three questions?

themes.title: The End Times
themes.description: Three weeks reading what scripture says about the return of Christ, the resurrection, the judgment, and the new creation. Christians read some of these passages in different ways; this plan gives you the passages themselves.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God that his kingdom outlasts every other.
core_arc.ask_seed: What is the stone that strikes the statue in Nebuchadnezzar's dream?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Worship the one given dominion and glory and a kingdom.
core_arc.ask_seed: Who is the one like the Son of man in Daniel's vision?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray as Daniel did, confessing and asking for mercy.
core_arc.ask_seed: How have Christians understood the seventy weeks of Daniel 9?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for the hope of resurrection.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Daniel 12 say about resurrection?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for the day when weeping is heard no more.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Isaiah's picture of the new heavens and new earth promise?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray: let the Lord be king over all the earth.
core_arc.ask_seed: What happens on the day of the Lord in Zechariah 14?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for a steady heart that is not alarmed.
core_arc.ask_seed: What signs does Jesus describe, and what does he tell his disciples to do about them?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to be found faithful in what is in front of you.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus say no one knows the day or the hour?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to see Christ in the least of these.
core_arc.ask_seed: On what basis does the King separate the sheep from the goats?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for strength to stand before the Son of man.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus tell his followers to do while they wait?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for the promise the angels gave.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do the angels promise about Jesus's return?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Give thanks for the victory over death.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Paul teach about the resurrection body?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for someone who is grieving, with this hope.
core_arc.ask_seed: What comfort does Paul give about those who have died in Christ?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to love the truth.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Paul say must happen before the day of the Lord?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for his patience, with you and with the world.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Peter say the Lord seems slow to keep his promise?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hear him say: fear not.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does John describe the risen Christ in Revelation 1?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Join the song: worthy is the Lamb.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is the Lamb the only one worthy to open the scroll?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for believers who suffer for their faith.
core_arc.ask_seed: Who is the great multitude in Revelation 7?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for endurance and faithfulness.
core_arc.ask_seed: How have Christians understood the beasts of Revelation 13?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Worship the one called Faithful and True.
core_arc.ask_seed: What are the main ways Christians have understood the thousand years in Revelation 20?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the last prayer of the Bible: even so, come, Lord Jesus.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the new Jerusalem show about where the story of scripture ends?

themes.title: Preparing for Fasting
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Formative, not tracking. Why fast, what fasting IS in scripture, who fasted and how. No counters; this is a heart-orientation.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Notice Jesus says 'when you fast,' not 'if.' Pray about your assumptions.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus assume fasting rather than command it?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the chapter. What is the fast that God actually wants from you this season?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Isaiah tie fasting to justice rather than only to private piety?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for a 'rent heart' before any rent garment.
core_arc.ask_seed: What is the difference between rending garments and rending hearts?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with the fact that the Spirit led Jesus into the fast, not out of it.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Luke specify Jesus was 'led by the Spirit' into the wilderness?

themes.title: A Scriptural View of Giving
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. The why and posture of giving in scripture. Formative; no ledger, no counters.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Where is your giving begrudging? Pray about that, not about the amount.
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul says God loves a cheerful giver. Is that a threat or a permission?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: What does proportional generosity look like for you?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus single out the widow's two coins over the larger gifts?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read about the early church. What does this raise in you?
core_arc.ask_seed: Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed, and Arminian traditions each read Acts 2 differently. How?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Identify one concrete act of love this week. Don't tell anyone you did it.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does John insist on love 'in deed' alongside love 'in word'?

themes.title: Genesis 1-11
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. The primeval narratives — creation, fall, flood, scattering. Foundational stories Israel told about God, humanity, and the world.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the seven days. Notice the rhythm 'and it was good.'
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the creation account culminate in rest, not in humanity?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about your own embodiment today, not in the abstract.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why are there two creation accounts, and how do Christian traditions read them together?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hear God's question — 'where are you?' — addressed to you today.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does God ask a question he already knows the answer to?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for the relationship most strained in your life.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Cain's offering get rejected? The text leaves it ambiguous — what do traditions do with that?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with the long flood narrative. What does it cost God?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the flood end with a covenant signed in the sky?

themes.title: Comfort in Grief
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Scripture's lament tradition meeting grief without hurrying it.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read slowly. Don't rush to verse 22.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does scripture include lament that does not resolve?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Tell God what you are not done grieving for.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus weep when he knows what is about to happen?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray it as it is. Don't add a hopeful coda the psalm refuses.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean that the only psalm without resolution is still scripture?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hold a hope you cannot yet feel. Sit with it for a minute.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the new creation begin with the absence of tears, specifically?

themes.title: Holy Week
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Palm Sunday through Easter Vigil. The dense, slow week of the gospel.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hear the crowd's hosanna. Pray it as your own.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus enter on a donkey?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Be the one Jesus stoops to.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does foot-washing replace the supper in John's account?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray honestly about what you do not want.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean for Jesus to pray the same prayer three times?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read it without commentary today. Don't move past it quickly.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is the day of crucifixion called 'good'?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit in the in-between day. No assignment.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Holy Saturday teach the church about waiting?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hear your name spoken by the risen Christ.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Mary not recognize him until he says her name?

themes.title: Through John
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. The fourth gospel — signs, 'I am' sayings, and the long discourses of Jesus.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the prologue out loud, slowly.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does John open in the beginning, before the manger?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about a place in your life where you keep going back to a 'well' that doesn't fill you.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus reveal his identity to a Samaritan woman first?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray to be fed.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed, and Arminian readers each emphasize about John 6?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with 'Jesus wept' before any miracle.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus weep when he knows what he is about to do?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Imagine being the one Jesus stoops to.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the foot-washing replace the institution of the supper in John?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray verses 20-21 — that you are inside what Jesus prays for.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus' prayer for 'oneness' mean across Christian traditions?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Receive a restoration you didn't earn.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus ask Peter the same question three times?

themes.title: Lent
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Forty days of return. Repentance not as scolding but as homecoming.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for a soft heart.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Joel locate repentance in heart-rending, not garment-rending?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray verses 10-12 over yourself today.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does David ask God to 'create' a clean heart?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with Jesus in his hunger.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Lent begin with wilderness?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the parable. Where are you in the story today?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the father run?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hear the invitation: come, eat, drink, return.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is Lent's repentance described as a banquet?

themes.title: The Miracles of Jesus
themes.description: Three weeks with the signs and wonders of Jesus: water into wine, storms stilled, the sick healed, the dead raised, and the empty tomb.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for joy, and for the quiet ways he provides.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does John call this the first of Jesus's signs?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Tell Jesus where you have worked all night and caught nothing.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Peter fall at Jesus's knees after the catch of fish?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bring to Jesus the people you know who are sick.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does this passage show about the authority of Jesus?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the leper's words: if you will, you can make me clean.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why did it matter that Jesus touched the leper?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Carry a friend to Jesus in prayer, as the four carried theirs.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus forgive the man's sins before he heals him?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for faith that takes Jesus at his word.
core_arc.ask_seed: What did Jesus find remarkable about the centurion's faith?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God that he sees those who grieve.
core_arc.ask_seed: What moved Jesus to raise the widow's son?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Name the storm you are in, and ask him to speak into it.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do the disciples learn about Jesus when he calms the storm?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for someone who seems beyond help.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus send the healed man home instead of letting him follow?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Reach for him in prayer the way the woman reached for his garment.
core_arc.ask_seed: How are the two healings in this passage connected?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Hear his question as yours: do you want to be made well?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus ask the man whether he wants to be healed?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Offer God the little you have for today.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the feeding of the five thousand show about who Jesus is?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray Peter's short prayer: Lord, save me.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Peter begin to sink?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask boldly, like the mother who would not be turned away.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the Syrophoenician woman's answer show about her faith?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to see clearly what you now see only in part.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why might Jesus have healed this blind man in two stages?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the father's prayer: I believe; help my unbelief.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does this passage teach about faith and prayer?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for whatever you can now see that you once could not.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus say about why the man was born blind?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Go back and give thanks for one thing he has done.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus point out that only the Samaritan came back?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bring your grief to the one who wept at the tomb.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why did Jesus wait two days before going to Lazarus?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Answer his question: what do you want me to do for you?
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Bartimaeus show about how to come to Jesus?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Praise him: he is not here, but is risen.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is the resurrection the greatest of the signs?

themes.title: The Parables of Jesus
themes.description: Two weeks in the stories Jesus told about the kingdom of God: the sower, the good Samaritan, the lost son, and more.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask God to make your heart good soil for his word.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do the four soils stand for in the parable of the sower?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for the small beginnings he grows.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do the mustard seed and the leaven teach about the kingdom?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to see the kingdom as worth everything.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the man sell all he has for the field?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask God to show you who is on your road today.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Jesus answer the question, who is my neighbor?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Keep asking for the thing you have nearly stopped praying about.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does this parable teach about asking God?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for what you have, and hold it with open hands.
core_arc.ask_seed: What was the rich man's mistake?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Say yes to his invitation today.
core_arc.ask_seed: Who ends up at the banquet, and why?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God that he searches until he finds.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do these two parables show about how God sees the lost?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Come home in prayer, whichever brother you are today.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the father's welcome show about God?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to notice who is at your gate.
core_arc.ask_seed: What is the warning in the story of the rich man and Lazarus?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the tax collector's prayer: God, be merciful to me a sinner.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why did the tax collector go home justified rather than the Pharisee?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Remember how much you have been forgiven.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is the first servant's debt so large in this parable?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God that his grace is not wages.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why do the workers who came last receive the same pay?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Offer back to God what he has placed in your hands.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the master expect of each servant?

themes.title: Through Philippians
themes.description: A slow walk through Paul's letter from prison — joy, partnership, the mind of Christ, and what it means to learn contentment.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray Paul's prayer (vv. 9-11) for someone you're partnered with in faith.
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul writes from prison. How does his greeting reflect — or not reflect — his circumstances?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Where in your week does the gospel seem 'stuck'? Tell God what you see.
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul says some preach Christ from envy or rivalry, and he rejoices anyway. What does that show about his loyalties?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: 'To live is Christ, to die is gain.' Read it slowly, then pray honestly about which feels closer today.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Paul prefer to depart but choose to remain?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Where does your conduct most need to 'become' the gospel today?
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul says suffering for Christ is 'granted' as a gift. How can suffering be a gift without that being a cliché?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the Christ hymn (vv. 6-11) aloud. Whose interests are you tempted to count above your own this week?
core_arc.ask_seed: What do Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed, and Arminian readers each tend to highlight in the kenosis hymn?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray verse 13 — 'God works in you to will and to do.' Name one thing you've been trying to do alone.
core_arc.ask_seed: How can Paul say 'work out your own salvation' AND 'God works in you' in the same breath?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit with the names — Timothy, Epaphroditus. Who carries your faith with you?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Paul spend so much of a short letter on personal news and named friends?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: What credentials are you holding? Hand one to Christ today, even loosely.
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul calls his pedigree 'rubbish.' Is he denying his story or reordering it?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about something behind you you keep looking at. Ask for the grace to press on without contempt for the past.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean that Paul has not yet 'attained' even after all his ministry?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Where do you act, today, as someone whose true citizenship is elsewhere?
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul cries when describing 'enemies of the cross.' Why grief and not anger?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Make a prayer that's mostly thanks today, then add one anxiety at the end.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does 'be careful for nothing' come right after a call to gentleness?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: List the eight Phil 4:8 attributes. Choose one to look for today.
core_arc.ask_seed: Is Paul prescribing positive thinking? If not, what?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about a place of plenty AND a place of want in your life right now.
core_arc.ask_seed: Paul says he 'learned' contentment. What does that imply about how it comes?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for someone whose generosity has reached you — name them.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Paul frame the Philippians' gift as 'fruit that abounds to your account'?

themes.title: Prayer Foundations
themes.description: Two weeks learning to pray with scripture as a teacher — the Lord's Prayer, the Psalms, and Jesus' own habits of prayer.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the Lord's Prayer slowly, one phrase per breath. Notice which one your heart catches on.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus give a model prayer rather than just 'pray more'?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for one thing today. Don't dress it up.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the disciple ask 'teach us to pray' after watching Jesus pray, not before?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Find a place that's quiet and private. Pray for one minute. That counts.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Mark mention the time of day when describing Jesus' prayer?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the psalm as your own this morning, even if not all of it fits.
core_arc.ask_seed: How is praying a psalm different from making up your own words?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Sit in silence for two minutes. Let the Spirit groan on your behalf.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean that we don't know what to pray for as we ought?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray your own 'how long?' to God. Don't end it neatly.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is it permissible — even biblical — to complain to God?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: No assignment. Read the psalm and rest in praise.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is praise its own discipline, distinct from petition?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the publican's prayer in your own words: 'God, be merciful to me.'
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus contrast two pray-ers and not just describe a good one?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the prayer slowly. Notice that you, today, are inside what Jesus prays for.
core_arc.ask_seed: Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed, and Arminian readers all treasure John 17. What does each tradition emphasize?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray 'create in me a clean heart' as a request, not as a confession of failure.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does David ask God to create rather than to fix?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Try one short phrase today, prayed at intervals — 'Lord, have mercy' is enough.
core_arc.ask_seed: Is 'pray without ceasing' realistic? What posture is Paul actually describing?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray something honest about what you do not want today, then add 'nevertheless, not my will.'
core_arc.ask_seed: Jesus prays the same thing three times. What does that say about what 'God's will be done' costs?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Approach prayer today as someone who is welcomed, not someone who is auditioning.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is the throne of grace described as a place to approach 'with confidence' specifically?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray verse 2 as a small commitment: 'every day will I bless thee.'
core_arc.ask_seed: Why end this challenge with a psalm of unbroken praise?

themes.title: Psalms of Ascent
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Psalms 120-134, the pilgrim psalms sung on the way up to Jerusalem.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray your honest distress.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the pilgrimage begin in trouble, not in arrival?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Look up. Literally. Pray verse 1 outside if you can.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the keeper not slumber or sleep mean for someone whose own sleep is broken?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for the peace of a particular place.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is gladness about going to worship its own discipline?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Wait on God like a servant on a master, not like a child wanting a thing.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the simile of servant-eyes teach about prayer?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Name a deliverance you didn't engineer. Thank God for it.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the psalm imagine the alternative — what would have happened — instead of moving on?

themes.title: Sermon on the Mount
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Matthew 5-7, Jesus' sustained teaching about the kingdom way.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the Beatitudes slowly. Which one names where you actually are today?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why begin with blessing instead of command?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about being salt where you are, today, in one specific place.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean for righteousness to 'exceed' the scribes' and Pharisees'?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pick one 'you have heard / but I say' that lands hard. Sit with it.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus intensify rather than relax the law?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Do something good today no one will see. Don't tell anyone.
core_arc.ask_seed: What is the difference between hiddenness and dishonesty?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: What treasure is your treasure right now? Pray honestly about that.
core_arc.ask_seed: How is the antidote to anxiety described — and how is it not?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Notice a beam in your own eye before naming a mote in someone else's.
core_arc.ask_seed: Is Jesus prohibiting all judgment, or a particular kind?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about the foundation of your life — sand or rock — without shame.
core_arc.ask_seed: What separates the wise builder from the foolish one?

themes.title: The Teachings of Jesus
themes.description: Three weeks listening to what Jesus taught, in his own words: the Sermon on the Mount, the greatest commandment, the new birth, and his last words to his disciples.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read the blessings slowly. Thank God for the one you most need to hear today.
core_arc.ask_seed: Who does Jesus call blessed, and why would that have surprised the crowd?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask God to show you where you keep a rule but miss its heart.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus mean when he says he came to fulfill the law, not abolish it?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray the Lord's Prayer line by line, pausing after each one.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus stress doing these things in secret?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Name what you are anxious about, and place each thing before the Father.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Jesus connect what we treasure with what we worry about?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for what you need. Jesus says to ask, seek, and knock.
core_arc.ask_seed: What is the difference between the wise and the foolish builder?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for love toward God, and toward one person by name.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus join love for God and love for neighbor into one answer?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for his love for the world, and for you in it.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus mean by being born again?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bring your own thirst to Jesus as honestly as the woman at the well did.
core_arc.ask_seed: What is the living water Jesus offers the Samaritan woman?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for someone who has wronged you, by name if you can.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus tell his followers to love their enemies?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Come to God today as a child comes: without a case to make.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean to become like a little child in the kingdom of heaven?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask God whether there is a debt you are still holding against someone.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the parable of the unforgiving servant teach about forgiveness?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for what you have, and ask what it is for.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus mean by being rich toward God?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Answer Jesus's question for yourself: who do you say that he is?
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean to deny yourself and take up your cross?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask God what you would find hardest to leave behind.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why did Jesus tell this man to sell everything he had?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for a chance to serve someone today without being noticed.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Jesus redefine greatness?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask Jesus for the food that lasts.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus mean when he calls himself the bread of life?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Rest in being known by name. Pray Psalm 23 if you know it.
core_arc.ask_seed: What marks the good shepherd in this passage?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank Jesus for stooping to serve, and ask whose feet you are to wash.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why did Jesus wash his disciples' feet?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bring your troubled heart to the one who said, let not your heart be troubled.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus mean by saying he is the way, the truth, and the life?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray simply to remain in him today.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean to abide in the vine?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank him for the promise: I am with you always.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus send his disciples to do in the Great Commission?

themes.title: Strength in Temptation
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Scripture treats temptation as expected, not shameful.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: What part of you most relates to which temptation in this passage?
core_arc.ask_seed: Why is each of Jesus' answers a quotation from scripture?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about a temptation you thought was uniquely yours.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Paul start by saying temptation is 'common'?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Approach Jesus today as someone who knows.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it cost the high priest to be 'tempted in every way'?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Tell God the honest version of the struggle today, in Paul's tone.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Paul put this confession in present tense?

themes.title: Topical Study: Faith
themes.description: Ten days on what faith is and what it looks like, from Abraham to the letter to the Hebrews.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for those who believed before you.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Hebrews 11 define faith?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bring to God a promise you find hard to believe.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why was Abraham's faith counted to him as righteousness?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for trust in the God who provides.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the testing of Abraham show about faith?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray Habakkuk's words: yet I will rejoice in the Lord.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean that the just shall live by faith?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Take Jesus at his word about one thing today.
core_arc.ask_seed: What did Jesus admire in the centurion's faith?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray: Lord, save me.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Peter's walk on the water teach about faith and doubt?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for whoever first brought you the word.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does faith come, according to Romans 10?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God that salvation is his gift.
core_arc.ask_seed: How do grace, faith, and works relate in Ephesians 2?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask what your faith is asking you to do today.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does James mean when he says faith without works is dead?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Fix your eyes on Jesus, and lay one weight down.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does the great cloud of witnesses help us run the race?

themes.title: Topical Study: Forgiveness
themes.description: Ten days on God's forgiveness of us, and ours of one another.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Stop keeping silent: tell God what you have been hiding.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does David say happened when he stopped hiding his sin?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray this psalm as your own.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does David ask God for in Psalm 51?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Bless the Lord, and forget not all his benefits.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Psalm 103 describe God's forgiveness?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God that he delights in mercy.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do Isaiah and Micah say about how fully God forgives?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank Jesus as someone who has been forgiven much.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus say the woman loved much?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Come home in prayer.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the father's welcome show about forgiveness?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask God about the debt you are still counting.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does seventy times seven mean?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Confess plainly, and receive what he promises.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does Jesus connect being forgiven with forgiving others?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for someone who meant you harm.
core_arc.ask_seed: How was Joseph able to forgive his brothers?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for a tender heart toward one person today.
core_arc.ask_seed: What reason does Paul give for forgiving one another?

themes.title: Topical Study: The Holy Spirit
themes.description: Two weeks on who the Holy Spirit is and what he does, from creation to Pentecost to the life of the believer.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank the Spirit who gives life and breath.
core_arc.ask_seed: What role does the Spirit of God have in creation?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask God to breathe on what seems dead.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does God promise to do by his Spirit in Ezekiel 36 and 37?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God that his Spirit is poured out on all kinds of people.
core_arc.ask_seed: Who receives the Spirit in Joel's prophecy?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Worship the one anointed to preach good news to the poor.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the Spirit do in the baptism and first sermon of Jesus?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for new life you could not give yourself.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean to be born of the Spirit?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask the Comforter to bring to mind what Jesus has said.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does Jesus promise the Spirit will do for his disciples?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask to be guided into truth today.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus say it is better for his disciples that he goes away?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for the church to speak plainly of the works of God.
core_arc.ask_seed: What happened on the day of Pentecost?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for your own church by name.
core_arc.ask_seed: What did life look like for the first believers after Pentecost?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Call on God as Father.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean to walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: When you have no words, rest in the Spirit who prays for you.
core_arc.ask_seed: How does the Spirit help us when we do not know how to pray?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Thank God for a gift you see in someone else.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does the Spirit give different gifts to different people?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Ask for the fruit you most lack.
core_arc.ask_seed: What is the fruit of the Spirit?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Give thanks to God for everything you can name.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does it mean to be sealed with the Spirit and filled with the Spirit?

themes.title: Rest for the Weary
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Scripture's vocabulary for rest, addressed to the worn-out.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Receive the invitation today. Do less, not more.
core_arc.ask_seed: Jesus offers a yoke as rest. Why is that not a contradiction?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Schedule a small withdrawal today — even fifteen minutes.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus pull the disciples away when there's still work to do?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray about your sleep. Treat it as belonging to God.
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the psalm mean by 'vain' striving?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: What are you waiting on? Pray it as a posture, not a delay.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Isaiah pair waiting with strength?

themes.title: Engaging Scripture
themes.description: Draft — pending editorial. Learning to read the Bible as scripture, not just as a text.

core_arc.prayer_prompt: What would 'meditating day and night' look like in your week — small and real?
core_arc.ask_seed: What does the psalm mean by 'meditating' on scripture?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pick one verse to memorize this week. Don't worry about the rest.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does this psalm describe scripture in so many different ways?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Read scripture today the way the Emmaus pair did — listening for the one being explained.
core_arc.ask_seed: Why does Jesus go through the whole canon before breaking the bread?

core_arc.prayer_prompt: Pray for one of the four uses Paul names: teaching, reproof, correction, training.
core_arc.ask_seed: What do Catholic, Orthodox, Reformed, and Arminian readers each emphasize about 'God-breathed' scripture?
